title: Euler's formula, geometrically
content: Euler's 1765 relation $OI^2 = R^2 - 2Rr$ between the circumcenter $O$, incenter $I$, circumradius $R$ and inradius $r$. The parent entry `oq-06` proved Euler's inequality $R \ge 2r$ purely in the side-length algebraic model; this file upgrades it to the **genuine geometric** statement, with $O$, $I$, and the vertices $A,B,C$ honest points of a real inner-product space and $OI^2$ their honest squared Euclidean distance. The strategy: place $O$ anywhere, work with position vectors $u=A-O$, $v=B-O$, $w=C-O$ of common length $R$, and reduce everything to one Gram-matrix expansion.

title: Setup: an arbitrary real inner-product space
content: Imports the inner-product basics, the tactic library, and the parent `Proofs.HeronsFormulaOQ06` (reusing its `circumradius`, `inradius`, `area`, `semiperimeter` definitions). The work is carried out over an arbitrary `F` with `[NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F]` — so the result is dimension-free, holding in the plane, in space, or in any real Hilbert space.
mathContext: $F$ a real inner-product space; $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{\mathbb{R}}$ the real inner product.

title: The Gram-expansion core
content: `weighted_sum_norm_sq` is the entire geometric content. For three vectors $u,v,w$ of common norm $R$ with pairwise distances $a=\|v-w\|$, $b=\|w-u\|$, $c=\|u-v\|$, it proves $\|a\,u + b\,v + c\,w\|^2 = R^2(a+b+c)^2 - abc(a+b+c)$. The three Gram inner products are read off from the polarization identity (`norm_sub_sq_real`) as $\langle u,v\rangle = R^2 - c^2/2$ and cyclic variants; expanding the squared norm via `inner_add/smul` lemmas, normalizing reversed entries with `real_inner_comm`, and substituting leaves a polynomial identity that `ring` closes — the cross terms collapsing to $-abc(a+b+c)$ by symmetric cancellation.
mathContext: $\langle u,v\rangle = R^2 - \tfrac{c^2}{2};\quad \|a u + b v + c w\|^2 = R^2(a{+}b{+}c)^2 - abc(a{+}b{+}c).$

title: The Euler core: OI² = R² − abc/(a+b+c)
content: `incenter_dist_circumcenter_sq` passes from points to position vectors $u=A-O$, $v=B-O$, $w=C-O$ (each of norm $R$ since $\mathrm{dist}\,O\,\cdot = R$), translates the side lengths into vector norms, and shows the key affine cancellation $I - O = (a+b+c)^{-1}\,(a\,u + b\,v + c\,w)$ — proved by the `module` tactic after noting the weights sum to $a+b+c$. Then $OI^2 = \|I-O\|^2$ is computed with `norm_smul` and the Gram core, and `field_simp` yields the area-free, square-root-free identity $OI^2 = R^2 - abc/(a+b+c)$.
mathContext: $I - O = \dfrac{a u + b v + c w}{a+b+c},\qquad OI^2 = R^2 - \dfrac{abc}{a+b+c}.$

title: The algebraic bridge 2Rr = abc/(a+b+c)
content: `two_circumradius_mul_inradius`: in the side-length model, $2 \cdot R \cdot r = abc/(a+b+c)$. Unfolding $R = abc/(4\,\mathrm{Area})$, $r = \mathrm{Area}/s$ and $s = (a+b+c)/2$, the area cancels — `field_simp` (using $\mathrm{Area} > 0$ from `area_pos`) and `ring` finish. This is the only place the area appears, and it disappears immediately; it is the bridge between the geometric core and the named $R^2 - 2Rr$ form.

title: Euler's triangle formula OI² = R² − 2Rr
content: `euler_OI_sq` is the headline: with $O,I,A,B,C$ honest points, $R = $ `circumradius a b c`, and $I$ the barycentric incenter, $OI^2 = R^2 - 2Rr$. The proof simply chains the Euler core (`incenter_dist_circumcenter_sq`) with the bridge (`two_circumradius_mul_inradius`), substituting $abc/(a+b+c) = 2Rr$ into $R^2 - abc/(a+b+c)$.

title: Euler's inequality as a sign of distance
content: `euler_inequality_of_dist`: since $OI^2 \ge 0$ (it is a squared distance, `sq_nonneg`) and $R > 0$ (`positivity` after unfolding `circumradius`), Euler's formula $OI^2 = R^2 - 2Rr$ forces $R \ge 2r$ — closed by `nlinarith`. This is the geometric content Euler gave the inequality in 1765: $R \ge 2r$ is not an algebraic estimate but the manifest nonnegativity of an actual squared distance, with equality exactly when $O = I$ (the equilateral case).
